> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2487558747e0f64e88587bde0fbd60373da6e75f` — the merge of head `11fac6c95544408a05b44aa5a5e71e9f7ce0e1d8` into base `55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2487558747e0f64e88587bde0fbd60373da6e75f && git checkout 2487558747e0f64e88587bde0fbd60373da6e75f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6 11fac6c95544408a05b44aa5a5e71e9f7ce0e1d8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6 && git merge --no-ff 11fac6c95544408a05b44aa5a5e71e9f7ce0e1d8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55382dc02a2168585a024ba142b98d8bce9910e6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `11fac6c95544408a05b44aa5a5e71e9f7ce0e1d8`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed against: card #22773 (body and all five comments; the seat's ACCEPT `6111057759` read as a claim to verify), ruling A on #22757 (director record `6105447950`, read at its source), the contract `packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts` on `origin/main`, PR #22864's body, file list and net diff against merge base `55382dc02a` (15 files, +1196 / -21), and the 39 check-runs on this head: 33 success, 6 skipped (opt-in or path-filtered), 0 failed, 0 pending. Test Core x7, TypeScript Type Check x5, Dogfood Regression Gate x4 (real showcase boot), Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset x2, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, the four PR-shape guards, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Core, Check Documentation Links and Flag docs are all green. No governed path in the file list; no `packages/spec` and no `packages/triggers/trigger-api` file.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged right or wrong:

1. **`isAuthGateAllowlisted(rawPath, method?)` and `evaluateAuthGate(user, path, method?)` gain an optional trailing method — RIGHT, and no existing caller's answer moves.** The exact-row half (`matchesAllowlistedRoute`) is byte-identical and still decides first; the parameterised half answers null unless a method string is passed (`matchParameterisedRoute`). Callers read on the head: REST `enforceAuth` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2373`) passes the path only, so its answer is unchanged; the dispatcher's `enforceAuthGate` now passes the method, and for a gated session that moves exactly one (path, method) class: `POST` on the four-segment hook route, unscoped or under one `/environments/:id` scope, which ruling A directs (the signature is the only credential, equal to the self-hosted mount, which has no gate). Pinned by the BOUNDARY sweep in `auth-gate.test.ts`: a corpus of every path to five segments over a ten-token vocabulary plus the six-segment scoped shape, six methods including none, judged against a transcription of the pre-row predicate; newly gated is the empty set, newly exempt is exactly the expected set built independently of the predicate. PIN 2's control: the six exact rows and the `auth` prefix stay exempt with a method or without.

2. **New export `matchInboundHookRoute(path, method)` and type `InboundHookRouteMatch` from `@objectstack/core` (`security/index.ts`) — RIGHT.** Additive. It is the one reading the row matches through, and the three runtime readers (the `/automation` floor's branch, the ADR-0069 gate through `isAuthGateAllowlisted`, the membership skip) ask it, so "admitted" and "served" cannot diverge on a spelling: the row-equals-reading identity is pinned in core, and the admitted-iff-served relation is pinned on the wire over 25 spellings for an anonymous caller and for a gated session, with 9 admitted and the rest refused before the member. Parameters come back raw and the serving domain decodes them (the `/meta` precedent), an undecodable escape passed raw — pinned. Exporting from core is the only way to have one reading without a core-to-runtime cycle.

3. **The `/automation` floor now passes `path: routePath` to `shouldDenyAnonymous` — RIGHT, and no pre-existing allow-list row can exempt any `/automation/...` spelling.** `routePath` is `/automation` plus the domain's subpath (`req.path.substring(11)`), scope already stripped. In `matchesAllowlistedRoute` every exemption needs the first post-base segment to be `auth`, a scope word, or one of the six literals; with base `[]` that segment is `automation`, and with base `api` or `api/v1` the first segment fails the base test, so the exact rows answer false on every `/automation` path (the BOUNDARY corpus contains `/automation/health`-shaped and `/automation/api/v1/...`-shaped paths and records no move). The pathless guard still decides first (pinned in `anonymous-deny.test.ts`). The REST seam passes no path to this decision (`rest-server.ts:2383`, by its own comment) and the other eleven call sites on the head pass none, so this floor is the only seam whose answer the row can change.

4. **The parameterised row against ruling A condition 1 — RIGHT.** `INBOUND_HOOK_ROUTE = { segments: ['automation', 'hooks', ':flowName', ':hookId'], methods: ['POST'] }`; `rest.length !== route.segments.length` answers null, which pins the count; literals compare raw and case-sensitive (no percent-decoding: `/automation/%68ooks/f/h` and `/Automation/hooks/f/h` stay gated); no mount base (`/api/v1/automation/hooks/f/h` stays gated); the retired `projects` scope is refused; any empty segment refuses the whole spelling, stricter than the exact rows' drop-empty reading and the right direction (`//automation/hooks/f/h` would otherwise be admitted by the row and served by nothing, the spelling disagreement the segment-1 pointer `6106817103` asked to pin). The one optional `/environments/:id` scope is the dispatcher's own spelling (the ADR-0069 and membership gates run before the strip and see it; the floor sees it stripped), the same allowance the `/approvals/act` row carries, and the count after the scope is still four. The card's three (`/automation/hooks`, `/automation/hooks/x`, `/automation/hooks/x/y/z`), the bare domain, deeper counts, sibling literals and the domain's real routes at every depth are pinned gated at the predicate (PIN 3, PIN 4) and on the wire (17 paths x 5 methods answer the floor's `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, member never called; every non-POST on the exact route likewise). Nothing wider than the ruling's letter is admitted.

5. **The membership-gate skip — RIGHT.** `if (matchInboundHookRoute(path, method)) return null;` sits beside the `/approvals/act` skip, before the `environmentId` read, `POST` only, through the same reading. Pinned on a multi-tenant host: a signed-in non-member reaches the verifier on both spellings with zero `sys_environment_member` reads; the same caller is `403 PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED` with one membership read on `GET /automation/hooks/runs/r1` (a run read of a flow named `hooks`, the reason the row is POST-only), on GET and DELETE of the route, on `POST` to three- and five-segment hook-shaped paths, and on the empty-segment spelling. The contract's "a signed-in caller is judged exactly as an anonymous one" requires it; without the skip something would sit between the allow-list and the verifier for a signed-in sender.

6. **Condition 2, "nothing sits between the allow-list and the verifier" — RIGHT, measured on the hosted shape from the code on the head.** The hono catch-all hands `dispatch()` `{ request: c.req.raw }` and parses its `body` argument from `raw.clone()` (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:325` and `:791`; pinned by `hono-catch-all-raw-request.test.ts`, #22576). Inside `dispatch()`: the trailing-slash strip; the liveness carve-out (no match); `resolveRequestScope` (an anonymous sender resolves to no user; its only refusal is the authz-store outage `503`, an infrastructure fault, not a gate on this route); the ADR-0069 gate, exempt through the row; the membership gate, skipped through the same reading; the scope strip; the registry resolves `/automation` (segment match); the floor admits the POST through the row; the very next statement hands the match to `handleInboundHookRequest`, ahead of the run-read gate, the authoring gate and the `automation` service probe. That module reads no session, no signature header and no body: it resolves the `trigger-api` slot per request, checks member presence, refuses a body the transport already consumed as a sanitised `500` (a transport fault that would otherwise reach the sender as a bad signature; the `/webhooks/redeliver` shape), decodes the two segments and forwards `context.request` itself. The tripwire pin proves the `automation` and `security` services are never touched on the admitted path, with a control showing the tripwire fires on an ordinary request; the acceptance pin proves the member receives the transport's own `Request` object with the spaced body byte-exact and verifies it with core's `verifyHttpSignature`, the function `ApiTrigger.handleRequest` verifies with (`packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts:311` on `origin/main`).

7. **Condition 2, the #5519 ordering — RIGHT as far as the ruling's text reaches.** A non-POST on the route meets the floor's `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` with neither `automation` nor `trigger-api` composed, never a `501` (pinned). An unsigned POST is admitted by the row (the row reads path and method; it cannot read a signature, and the contract forbids a pre-check between the allow-list and the verifier) and meets the verifier's one `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`, the same answer for a wrong secret, a tampered body, a malformed header, an unknown flow and a wrong hook id (six cases pinned, member called each time, none accepted), so no route shape leaks past it. The residual the dev flagged, service presence on this route, is judged in ③.

8. **Route ledger, census and gates — RIGHT.** One `public` row for `POST /automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId` under domain `/automation`, tool-written census 86 to 87 (`check:route-ledger-census` green); the dogfood census pair moves 86 to 87 with `keys` 23 and `blindSpot` 0 (an existing domain key); the live-mount parity gate names the self-hosted raw-app door as the reason the port never answers the row; `check-route-envelope.mjs` declares `automation-hooks.ts` with `handBuilt: 0` (the member's `Response` goes back as `result`, every own refusal through `deps.error`). The Dogfood Regression Gate on this head booted the real showcase and is green.

9. **Route and surface ownership rules — RIGHT.** Rule 1: two doors on two shapes by the ruling's letter; the CONTROL pin shows the dispatcher plugin mounts nothing answering the path on a kernel with `http.server` (with a matcher control that does find the three-segment trigger door), and `dispatcher-plugin.ts` is untouched. Rule 3: absence answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (derived from the status by `apiErrorResponse`) naming the missing service or member and the remedy, read per request (a slot registered after a `501` is reached by the next request, pinned), never `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`, as the contract requires. Rule 5: not a `GET`, reads no `req.query`; the query rides inside the forwarded `Request` to the member exactly as the self-hosted mount receives it, so no closed set is owed by this domain. Prime Directive #13: ADR-0069, ADR-0056 D2 and ADR-0041 ids are in the code; the ADR-0076 anchor's invariant on `http-dispatcher.ts` (scope, then both gates, then the registry) holds, the skip living inside the membership gate and the hook branch inside the domain after its floor.

10. **Landing point (the recorded deviation) — RIGHT.** `createAutomationDomain` registers `prefix: '/automation'` with the default segment match, the registry is first-match, and `DomainRoute` cannot express `:flowName/:hookId`; a sibling registration would have to precede `/automation` and would leave the row unread by any anonymous floor, while the ruling says the row is honoured by the floor. `domains/automation.ts` is edited under the claim's conditional clause; `domain-handler-registry.ts` is untouched.

11. Observation, not a flag: `trigger-api` is not a key on `ServiceSlotContracts`, so the slot resolves through the untyped overload and the door casts to `Pick` of `ITriggerApiService`, exactly as the redeliver sibling does. Typing the key is a `packages/spec` matter the card bars for this segment.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22773-automation-hooks-domain.md`: `@objectstack/core` **minor**, `@objectstack/runtime` **minor** — matches what the diff publishes. Core: one new export (`matchInboundHookRoute`, `InboundHookRouteMatch`), two optional trailing parameters, one new exemption; nothing removed, no existing answer narrowed (BOUNDARY: newly gated is empty). Runtime: one new door and module, one new ledger row; nothing removed. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed (`check-adr-0087-registration` on the head: no declared-breaking changeset). `packages/qa/dogfood` is `private: true` and `scripts/` publishes nothing; `packages/spec` is untouched, so no artifact regeneration is owed. The changeset body's sentences were checked against the diff: the method semantics on both functions, the forwarding in `shouldDenyAnonymous`, the raw-segment export, the two `501`s and the sanitised `500`s, and the self-hosted-unchanged claim (the CONTROL pin). Check Changeset is green on the head.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — one exact parameterised `POST` route passes the ADR-0069 gate, the `/automation` anonymous floor and the membership gate with no session, as ruling A directs; the precedent is the `['approvals', 'act']` row declared `yes` on #22577. `yes` takes at least minor; both packages are minor.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and open question from `os-dev-report` `6110990230`, answered:

- **Deviation: the route is handed off inside the `/automation` domain, not registered as a sibling `DomainRoute`.** Right, for the reasons in ① item 10. Accepted.
- **`packages/qa/http-conformance` untouched; the end-to-end leg on the real member is owed by whichever of #22773 and #22774 lands second.** Accepted per the triage unlock `6107344979`: #22774's member is not on `main` (`origin/main` registers no `trigger-api` service), and the double verifies with the same core function the trigger uses. Owed by the second lander, not a blocker on this head.
- **`git merge origin/main` before opening; the one-object `git fetch` for a self-test fixture; zero label writes; commit-trailer spelling; the acceptance notes written once.** Process notes with no contract bearing. Noted.
- **Out-of-scope finding: the six exact rows' scope reading (empty segments dropped, the retired `projects` scope accepted) admits `/environments//x/approvals/act` and `/projects/x/approvals/act`, spellings the dispatcher does not route, so a gated session gets `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` rather than `403` there.** Pre-existing, read from the code, not measured on the wire, and nothing is served on those spellings, so it is a 404-versus-403 dialect on a dead spelling, not a bypass: a note under Prime Directive #10, not a card. The new row refuses both by construction. No action owed on this head.
- **Open question: on a kernel with no `trigger-api` service, an anonymous unsigned POST to the exact route answers the contract's `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, and with the service the verifier's `401`, so an anonymous caller can tell whether a deployment composes the inbound-hook trigger. Is service presence inside condition 2's ordering?** Answered on the merits: **inside, as this segment is bound; option A stands; no change on this head.** (i) The #5519 ordering protects the 401-versus-501 fingerprint on paths an anonymous caller may not reach at all; on this route the anonymous sender is the intended caller by ruling A's letter, the row is `POST` only, and every other method still meets the floor before any probe (pinned). (ii) What the `501` discloses is composition, not route shape: a `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` confirms the same route exists, and the route is `public` in the ledger and in the contract's own docblock. (iii) The ruling's condition 2 names "the floor's refusal" for an unsigned request, but the floor reads path and method only; the only way to make an unsigned request meet the floor is a signature pre-check between the allow-list and the verifier, which the same condition ("nothing sits between") and the contract ("nor does the caller check, pre-filter or short-circuit the signature") both forbid, so the condition can only mean the boundary's refusal, which the unsigned POST meets. (iv) Ruling A's letter itself lists "an absent member" as a refusal class beside a bad signature and an unknown hook, and the spec segment (#22772, reviewed at this tier after the ruling, merged) fixed that class as "a typed 404 or 501, never `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`" with its reason: a signature refusal on a mis-composed deployment would tell a correctly signing sender its signature is wrong, which Route and surface ownership rule 3 (absence must be loud, naming the remedy) also forbids. (v) The two precedent doors, `/approvals/act` (anonymous, allow-listed) and `/webhooks/redeliver`, already answer `501` for an absent service. This PR implements the contract on `origin/main` as written. If the maintainer reads condition 2 as reaching service composition, that is option B: a contract amendment in `packages/spec` on #22757's thread for the `domain:spec` seat, then a one-line change in `domains/automation-hooks.ts`; a follow-up card, not a defect in this head, and this record does not order it.
